prompt.context: Your client is Hot Koala, a leading producer of outdoor lifestyle products (e.g., games, towels, chairs, umbrellas) based in Dubai. It is looking to make a 'splash' with its newest product line — the Polar Bear Pool Float (PBPF). Its current and loyal customer base is entirely in the Middle East, but it is strongly considering new market opportunities. The founder/CFO (Chief Fun Officer) is torn on where to launch the PBPF and has asked us how we would evaluate new geographies.
prompt.question: How would you evaluate new geographies for Hot Koala to launch the Polar Bear Pool Float?

clarifying_info.a: Hot Koala has several smaller, niche competitors, but none offer the breadth of products.

clarifying_info.q: Does Hot Koala sell outside the Middle East currently?
clarifying_info.a: No — its current and loyal customer base is entirely in the Middle East.

clarifying_info.q: What is Hot Koala's annual revenue?
How does Hot Koala currently sell its products?

exhibits.title: Four Primary Markets — Pool Float Market Data
exhibits.shows: A bubble chart comparing four geographies (USA, South Africa, Australia, UAE) on three dimensions: total industry floats sold in 2015 (x-axis, millions), year-over-year market growth rate (y-axis, %), and average price per float (bubble label). Bubble size may indicate relative market size.

exhibits.title: Production and Shipping Cost Structure — USA vs. UAE
exhibits.shows: A cost breakdown table listing per-float cost items for the USA and UAE markets. Shared COGS items (Materials, Labor, Packaging) apply to both. Market-specific line items include Shipping, Storage, Taxes, and Distribution Fees.

framework: Market attractiveness: market size (floats sold), growth rate (YoY), and pricing opportunity
Competitive landscape: existing competitors, Hot Koala's differentiation, brand recognition
Revenue potential: addressable market value = units x avg price
Cost structure: production/COGS, shipping, storage, taxes, distribution fees
Time to market and operational complexity: lead times, new distribution channel setup
Distribution channels: ecommerce vs. in-store mix by geography
Qualitative/regulatory factors: weather/pool access, intellectual property (trademarks/patents), taxes, import duties
Existing presence and brand recognition: Hot Koala already has Middle East brand equity

questions.prompt: Based on Exhibit 1, which two countries should Hot Koala prioritize and why? What other factors should be considered?
questions.guidance: Candidate should rank markets using market size, growth rate, and pricing. Strong answer directs to: USA for significant absolute market size (10M floats, $500M market); UAE for existing brand recognition in the Middle East, highest YoY growth (20%), and premium pricing potential ($99). Other factors to consider: production and shipping cost differences, taxes, IP restrictions (trademarks/patents), distribution channel fit (ecommerce vs. in-store), and reputation/brand recognition. Any two markets can be argued with good logic, but interviewer should guide candidate toward USA and UAE.

questions.prompt: What are the potential cost drivers for producing and shipping PBPFs to the US versus UAE? (Then calculate the unit cost for each market using Exhibit 2.)
questions.guidance: Candidate should brainstorm cost buckets first: COGS (materials, labor, packaging), shipping/logistics, storage/warehousing, taxes/duties, distribution/fulfillment fees. Then calculate unit costs from Exhibit 2.

math.setup: Convert rate-based costs to per-float figures, then sum all cost items per market.
steps: Shared COGS: Materials $15 + Labor $10 + Packaging $5 = $30/float (same for both markets)
USA Distribution Fees: 50% of storage fee per float = 0.5 x $4 = $2/float
math.answer: USA unit cost = $50/float; UAE unit cost = $40/float

questions.prompt: Hot Koala has initial inventory of 50,000 floats. If sold at a 10% premium over costs, what would its initial market share be in each target market (US and UAE)?
questions.guidance: Candidate must (1) calculate selling price at 10% margin over unit cost, (2) compute total revenue from 50k units, and (3) divide by total market revenue. A strong candidate will flag that in the US, the selling price equals the average market price ($55 vs. $50 average — actually $50 cost * 1.1 = $55), while in UAE the selling price ($44) is well below the market average ($99), indicating a strong margin expansion opportunity in UAE. Note: the casebook uses $99 ≈ $100 for UAE market value and rounds 250k floats to compute a $25M UAE market.

math.setup: Selling price = unit cost x 1.1. Revenue = 50,000 x selling price. Market size = industry floats sold x average market price. Market share = revenue / market size.
steps: US market size: 10,000,000 floats x $50 avg price = $500,000,000
UAE market size: 250,000 floats x $100 avg price (approx.) = $25,000,000
math.answer: US initial market share ≈ 0.55%; UAE initial market share ≈ 8.8%

brainstorming.prompt: What are the potential cost drivers when producing and shipping PBPFs from a Chinese manufacturer to the US and UAE?

categories.name: Logistics / Shipping
ideas: Ocean freight from China to destination
Air freight if faster delivery needed

categories.name: Storage / Warehousing
ideas: Third-party logistics (3PL) warehouse fees in the US

categories.name: Overhead
ideas: Compliance and legal costs for new geography

recommendation: Prioritize expanding in the UAE: Hot Koala already has brand recognition in the Middle East, the UAE market has the highest YoY growth (20%), premium pricing ($99 avg), and even at a 10% margin the client would capture ~8.8% market share — indicating significant room to grow before facing price pressure.

Enter the US market through an alternative/differentiated strategy: the US market is very large ($500M) but unit costs ($50) are at par with the average market selling price, making a standard 10% margin extremely thin. A differentiated, premium-positioned product or partnership strategy would be needed to compete.
risks: In the US, low margin at current cost structure — difficult to compete unless PBPF is highly differentiated and can command premium pricing above $50
UAE market is relatively small in absolute size (250k floats vs. 10M in US); growth ceiling may be reached quickly
Single Chinese manufacturer dependency creates supply chain concentration risk
Ecommerce-only channel may limit reach in markets where in-store purchase is dominant
Brand recognition outside the Middle East is currently zero — significant marketing investment required
next_steps: Conduct deeper pricing analysis in UAE to assess whether Hot Koala can position above the $99 average given brand differentiation
Explore US market entry via a premium sub-brand or licensing/partnership to reduce cost-to-serve
Evaluate alternative US distribution partners to reduce the $2/float distribution fee
Assess IP protection strategy (trademarks, patents) before entering new geographies
Pilot UAE expansion with initial 50k inventory and measure actual market share capture against the 8.8% projection
